title: How to change the sidebar in Finder on Mac: add, remove and reorder items
metaTitle: How to Change the Sidebar in Finder on Mac (Step by Step)
description: How to change the sidebar in Finder on Mac: show or hide it, edit Favorites, reorder items, and fix a missing section. Steps for current macOS.
targetKeyword: how to change the sidebar in finder on mac
intro: To change the sidebar in Finder on Mac, open Finder > Settings > Sidebar and tick or untick the items you want. To add a folder or disk, drag it into Favorites, and use View > Hide Sidebar or Option-Command-S (⌥⌘S) when you want the whole sidebar out of the way.
tldr: Show or hide the sidebar with View > Hide Sidebar or View > Show Sidebar, or press ⌥⌘S.
Pick which items appear in Finder > Settings > Sidebar, then tick or untick them.
Add a folder or disk by dragging it into Favorites. Hold ⌘ to add a file or app.
Remove an item by dragging it out until the Remove sign appears. The original file stays put.
If Show Sidebar is dimmed, choose View > Show Toolbar first.

blocks.text: The Finder sidebar is the column on the left side of every Finder window. It holds shortcuts to the places you use most, such as your Desktop, Documents, and external drives. Changing it means three things. You decide what shows, what order it shows in, and how much room it takes up on screen.
Show or hide the sidebar in Finder

The fastest way is the keyboard. Press Option-Command-S (⌥⌘S) while a Finder window is in front. Apple lists this shortcut as hiding or showing the sidebar in Finder windows. Press it again to bring the sidebar back. The same shortcut works in both directions, so you never need to hunt through a menu.

If you prefer the menu, click View in the menu bar. Choose View > Hide Sidebar to remove the sidebar. While it is hidden, the same menu offers View > Show Sidebar instead. Choose that item to bring the sidebar back on screen.
When Show Sidebar is greyed out

Sometimes View > Show Sidebar is dimmed, so you cannot click it. The toolbar is the usual cause. Apple says that hiding the toolbar also hides the sidebar. Choose View > Show Toolbar first. Then open the View menu again and pick Show Sidebar.

You can rearrange toolbar items by holding Command and dragging them. Apple's toolbar page covers that process. It is separate from the sidebar list, so only touch the toolbar if you want to change it.
Choose which items appear in the sidebar

The sidebar is a list of shortcuts. Each entry points to a place on your Mac or a connected disk. Apple calls these items aliases. You control the whole list from one pane. Open Finder > Settings, click Sidebar, then check the items you want and uncheck the rest.

Finder > Settings is where current Apple pages send you. Older guides say Finder > Preferences. The menu sits under the menu named Finder, just to the right of the Apple logo. If Settings is missing, make sure Finder is the active app, because the Finder menu only shows while Finder is in front.

The Settings window has four panes: General, Tags, Sidebar, and Advanced. You want the Sidebar pane. Each item in that pane is a checkbox. Ticked items show in the sidebar. Unticked items disappear from the list, but the folders themselves stay where they are.

Apple says the Sidebar pane also controls the quick-access items you see in Open and Save dialogs. That makes it worth a look if you often save files from other apps. A tidy list in Settings means a tidier list in those dialogs too.

blocks.title: Command-Comma from another app
blocks.text: Command-Comma (⌘,) opens settings for whichever app is in front. In Finder, that is Finder's Settings. In another app, it opens that app's settings instead.
Add a folder, disk, file or app to Favorites

Favorites is the section for places you open every day. You add to it by dragging. Open a Finder window, find the folder or disk, and drag it onto the Favorites section. Let go when the list shows it. Apple says this works for folders and disks.

Files and apps need one extra key. Hold the Command key before you start dragging, and keep it held until you drop the item into Favorites. Apple's instructions call this out for files and apps. Without Command, the drag is meant for folders and disks.
Example: a client folder

Say your client files live in Documents > Clients > Northwind. You open that folder, then drag it into Favorites. It appears in the sidebar, and one click takes you there from any Finder window. The folder itself stays where it is, because sidebar items are aliases.

Now say you also need one spreadsheet from the same project every week. Hold Command, then drag that file into Favorites. It sits beside the folder. This works well for a single file you open often, such as a budget or a list of invoices.
Reorder the items in the sidebar

Drag an item up or down inside the list to move it. Put the places you open most near the top. Move rarely used items toward the bottom. There is no separate ordering menu. The drag is the whole method.

A practical order for many people puts Desktop and Downloads at the top, the active project folder next, external drives after that, and rarely used places last. Check the order after a week. Move anything you have not touched since.
Remove an item without deleting the file
Drag the item out of the sidebar. Keep the mouse button or trackpad pressed, and move the pointer away from the list. Watch for the Remove sign. When it appears, let go. The alias leaves the sidebar.

blocks.title: Removing is not deleting
blocks.text: Dragging an item out of the sidebar only removes its shortcut. The folder, disk, or file stays where it was. To delete something, you still do that in its own location.
If you are not sure what an item is, open it first. Check where it lives in a Finder window. Then remove the alias. You can add it back with the drag from the earlier section.
Collapse, expand and resize the sidebar

Hover over a section heading in the sidebar. Show and Hide buttons appear beside it. Click Hide to fold that section away. Click Show to open it again. A folded section keeps a long list short without removing any items.

To change the width, drag the thin divider between the sidebar and the file list. Pull it right to widen the sidebar, so long folder names read more easily. Pull it left to give more room to the files.
Fix a missing Favorites section

Sometimes Favorites does not show at all. Apple's fix is to select at least one item in the Favorites section under Finder > Settings > Sidebar. Open that pane, find the Favorites list, and tick at least one item. The section should return to the sidebar.
Check the toolbar as well. If the toolbar is hidden, the sidebar is hidden with it. Choose View > Show Toolbar, then look at the sidebar again.
Common mistakes when changing the Finder sidebar

items: Looking for Finder > Preferences. Current Apple pages say Finder > Settings. Older guides may still use the old name.
Dragging a file or app without the Command key. Apple's instructions say to hold Command for files and apps.
Thinking removal deletes the file. Sidebar items are aliases, so the original stays where it is.
Hiding the toolbar and wondering where the sidebar went. Hiding the toolbar also hides the sidebar.
Pressing Command-Comma from another app. It opens that app's settings, not Finder's.

blocks.text: Those four cover most sidebar work. The path bar shortcut is worth knowing too. It shows the folder path in a Finder window, which helps when you are hunting for a file deep in a folder tree.

Command-1 through Command-4 switch the view of a Finder window. ⌘1 shows icons, ⌘2 list, ⌘3 columns, and ⌘4 gallery. Column view shows the sidebar and each level of folders side by side, so a tidy sidebar pairs well with it.
Which macOS version you are on

Finder's customizable sidebar has been around for a long time. Wikipedia says Mac OS X Panther (10.3) added it. The steps in this guide use current Apple naming, so they should match recent macOS releases.

Wikipedia lists macOS 27.0 as released on September 14, 2026, and Apple's keyboard shortcuts page carries that same date. No official Apple changelog I could open lists sidebar changes in macOS 27. If a menu name looks different on your Mac, check the Apple page that matches your version.
What to do after the sidebar looks right

Once the sidebar is set, check the Favorites list about once a month. Remove anything you no longer open. Add the new project folders you started since the last check. A short list is easier to scan, and it keeps Open and Save dialogs quick too.

faq.question: Can I hide the Finder sidebar completely?
faq.answer: Yes. Choose View > Hide Sidebar, or press Option-Command-S (⌥⌘S) while a Finder window is in front. Use View > Show Sidebar or the same shortcut to bring it back.

faq.question: Why is Show Sidebar greyed out in the View menu?
faq.answer: The toolbar is probably hidden. Hiding the toolbar also hides the sidebar, so Apple says to choose View > Show Toolbar first. Then choose View > Show Sidebar.

faq.question: Does removing a folder from the sidebar delete it?
faq.answer: No. Sidebar items are aliases. Dragging an item out until the Remove sign appears removes only the shortcut. The folder, disk, or file stays where it was.

faq.question: Why won't my file go into Favorites?
faq.answer: Files and apps need the Command key. Hold ⌘ while you drag the file or app into Favorites. Folders and disks go in with a plain drag.

faq.question: Do my sidebar choices change Open and Save dialogs?
faq.answer: Yes, according to Apple. The items you tick in the Sidebar pane also appear in Open and Save dialogs. Change them in Finder > Settings > Sidebar.

faq.question: Can I change the Finder sidebar on an iPhone or in a web browser?
faq.answer: This guide covers Finder on a Mac only. Apple's sidebar pages do not describe a web or iPhone version, so these steps do not apply there.

faq.question: Why does my menu say Preferences instead of Settings?
faq.answer: Older guides say Finder > Preferences. Apple's current pages say Finder > Settings. The sources do not confirm which release made the change, so use the name your Finder menu shows.

steps.name: Make Finder the active app
steps.text: Click any Finder window, or click the Finder icon in the Dock. Check that Finder is the active app. Its name appears in the menu bar at the top left, next to the Apple logo.

steps.name: Show or hide the sidebar
steps.text: Click View in the menu bar, then choose Hide Sidebar. The sidebar disappears. To bring it back, choose View > Show Sidebar, or press ⌥⌘S again.
steps.tip: If Show Sidebar is dimmed, go to View > Show Toolbar first.

steps.name: Open Finder Settings
steps.text: Click Finder in the menu bar, then choose Settings. Older guides say Preferences. Command-Comma opens the same window while Finder is the front app.

steps.name: Open the Sidebar pane
steps.text: Click Sidebar in the Settings window. The pane lists the items that can appear in the Finder sidebar and in Open and Save dialogs. Check each item you want. Uncheck the rest.

steps.name: Add a folder or disk to Favorites
steps.text: Open a Finder window, then drag the folder or disk into the Favorites section of the sidebar. Let go when the list shows it. The original folder or disk does not move.
steps.tip: Drop it inside the Favorites list, not on a file in the main window.

steps.name: Add a file or app to Favorites
steps.text: Hold the Command key, then drag the file or app into Favorites. Keep Command held until you drop it. Apple's instructions specify Command for these items.

steps.name: Reorder the items
steps.text: Drag an item up or down inside the sidebar. Drop it where you want it. Put the places you use most at the top.

steps.name: Remove an item
steps.text: Drag the item out of the sidebar until the Remove sign appears, then let go. Only the shortcut goes. The folder, disk, or file stays where it was.

steps.name: Bring back Favorites
steps.text: If Favorites is not visible, open Finder > Settings > Sidebar. Tick at least one item in the Favorites section. The section returns to the sidebar.

troubleshooting.problem: View > Show Sidebar is dimmed and will not click
troubleshooting.fix: Choose View > Show Toolbar first. Apple says hiding the toolbar also hides the sidebar, so the toolbar must be visible before the sidebar can return.

troubleshooting.problem: The Favorites section is missing from the sidebar
troubleshooting.fix: Open Finder > Settings > Sidebar. Tick at least one item in the Favorites list. Apple's fix relies on that selection to show the section.

troubleshooting.problem: I dragged a file into Favorites and nothing happened
troubleshooting.fix: Files and apps need the Command key. Hold ⌘ while you drag the file or app. Folders and disks do not need it.

troubleshooting.problem: I removed a folder and worry it is gone
troubleshooting.fix: Sidebar items are aliases. Removing one only removes the shortcut. Find the original folder in its usual location, where it should still be.

troubleshooting.problem: Settings is not in the Finder menu
troubleshooting.fix: Click a Finder window first so Finder is the active app. Older guides say Finder > Preferences, so check which name your menu shows.

troubleshooting.problem: The sidebar vanished after I changed the toolbar
troubleshooting.fix: Choose View > Show Toolbar. Hiding the toolbar also hides the sidebar, so the sidebar returns once the toolbar is visible.
